Oracle 19C installation document

What we need ?

1. A virtual machine
2. MobaxTERM
3. Oracle linux iso
4. Database installation file

Steps :

1. Install the vm upload the iso file

In this step you should give memory 4G , CPU 2core and also put the installation mode in GUI instead of minimal.

Give root password , create a normal user and give it a password.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Create groups

Groupadd oinstall

Groupadd dba

1. Create local repository

For accessing to the database offline and avoiding conflict in the 19c version we should create local repository.

For doing this first create a directory for the iso we already have:

'mkdir -p /ole7'

And import the iso file inside of it then create a file for mounting the iso file:

'mkdir -p /ole7_repo'

And then mount :

'sudo mount -o loop,ro /ole7/file.iso /ole7_repo'

Add this following line to the /etc/fstab file so when the db reboot the system always mount the DVD images:

/ole7/OracleLinux-R7-U8-Server-x86_64-dvd.iso /ole7_repo iso9660 loop,ro 0 0

Inside the yum.repos.d file in the etc open the text file for loe7 (/etc/ yum.repos.d/ol7.repo) add this following informations

name=OL7

baseurl=file:///ole7_repo

gpgkey=file:///etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY

gpgcheck=1

enabled=1

Clean up the yum cache

'yum clean all'

Now we should test to see that if we have access to the repository :  
'yum repolist'

```
6- add groups
groupadd -g 54321 oinstall
groupadd -g 54322 dba
groupadd -g 54323 oper
groupadd -g 54324 backupdba
groupadd -g 54325 dgdba
groupadd -g 54326 kmdba
groupadd -g 54327 asmdba
groupadd -g 54328 asmoper
groupadd -g 54329 asmadmin
groupadd -g 54330 racdba
7- create oracle user
useradd -u 54321 -g oinstall -G dba,oper oracle
passwd oracle
8- secure linux and then reboot
 vi /etc/selinux/config
add this following :
SELINUX=permissive
```

9- Directories and permissions

Enter as a root session.

Create home directory and make it save in all sessions.

mkdir -p /u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1

mkdir -p /u02/oradata

chown -R oracle:oinstall /u01 /u02

chmod -R 775 /u01 /u02

mkdir /home/oracle/scripts

10- bash_profile

Enter as oracle user and fill the bash_profile like this :

vi ~/.bash_profile

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Then exit and save it

resource ~/.bash_profile

```
11- Create a "start_all.sh" and "stop_all.sh" script that can be called from a startup/shutdown service. Make sure the ownership and permissions are correct.
```

vi /home/oracle/scripts/start_all.sh

# !/bin/bash

. /home/oracle/scripts/setEnv.sh

export ORAENV_ASK=NO

. oraenv

export ORAENV_ASK=YES

dbstart \\\$ORACLE_HOME

EOF

cat > /home/oracle/scripts/stop_all.sh <<EOF

# !/bin/bash

. /home/oracle/scripts/setEnv.sh

export ORAENV_ASK=NO

. oraenv

export ORAENV_ASK=YES

dbshut \\\$ORACLE_HOME

then give it permissions :

chown -R oracle:oinstall /home/oracle/scripts

chmod u+x /home/oracle/scripts/\*.sh

12- Installations

Cd \$ORACLE_HOME

./runInstaller

13-create database

Dbca

14-disable the firewall

Check the status :

Systemctl status firewall;

Disable :

systemctl stop firewalld.service

systemctl disable firewalld.service
